Introduction 
This document outlines everything you must complete before the CalderR Agentic 
AI Engineering Internship begins on Monday, 22 June 2026.  Two preparation days 
have been allocated, Friday 19 June and Saturday 20 June, for environment setup, 
foundational learning, and tool configuration. 
  
Arriving on Day 1 with a fully working environment means the cohort can focus on

building from the very first session.  Please treat these two days as your first 
professional obligation within the program. 
  
Objectives 
· Configure a complete local development environment 
· Install and verify all required software, tools, and libraries 
· Obtain and secure API credentials for all required services 
· Execute a successful end-to-end LLM call from your local machine 
· Establish your GitHub presence and understand version control expectations

· Complete the prerequisite self-assessment before June 22.

Key Concepts to Understand Before June 22: 
· Token: the unit of text a model reads and generates 
· Context window: the maximum number of tokens a model can process at once 
· Temperature: controls randomness; 0 = deterministic, 1+ = creative 
· System prompt: the instruction that defines the model's behaviour and persona 
· Completion vs Chat: the two API styles; this program uses the Chat format 
exclusively

exclusively 
· LangChain chain: a composable sequence of steps using the pipe ( | ) operator 
· Agent loop: the cycle an AI agent uses: receive input → reason → act with tools → 
observe → repeat

             Week # 1 
 
Hands-on Labs 
Complete all three labs over the course of the week. Each lab builds toward the skills 
required for your Friday project submission. 
  
Lab 1.1: Your First Groq Agent 
Build a Python CLI chatbot that: uses Groq llama-3-8b, maintains conversation 
history, supports /clear and /exit commands, and shows token usage per response. 
  
Lab 1.2: Manual ReAct Loop

Lab 1.2: Manual ReAct Loop 
Without using any framework, implement a ReAct agent that can: search a mock 
'database' of facts, calculate math expressions using eval(), and decide which tool to 
call based on the user's question. 
  
Lab 1.3: Prompt Engineering A/B Test 
Write five different system prompts for the same task (summarising news articles). 
Measure accuracy, conciseness, and tone. Document your findings in a brief report.
